A1.justification: Both PDFs present VisNumBench and include readable main text and Appendices A–D. Figures, tables, and appendix examples can be matched reliably despite layout changes and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original model evaluations, human accuracy measurements on 600 sampled questions, and manual analysis of 120 model errors.

after.justification: v2 retains those original empirical results and adds quantitative CoT-prompt evaluations in Table 9.

M1.justification: The benchmark construction, task design, and proposed evaluation framework remain unchanged. Newly documented answer extraction does not establish an actual method revision; the CoT addition is an experimental prompting condition.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 1,011 synthetic and 902 real-world questions, covering seven numerical attributes and four estimation tasks. Dataset sources and category counts are retained.

E2.justification: The evaluated model roster is unchanged, including mathematical, reasoning-tuned, and historical models. v2 Table 9 varies prompting for three existing models, while Table 13 consolidates previously evaluated models.

E3.justification: v2 adds a systematic CoT-prompt comparison for InternVL2.5-78B, Qwen2.5-VL-72B, and Gemini 2.0 Flash on both subsets. Table 8 distinguishes standard letter-only instructions from the CoT prompt. Newly disclosed preprocessing and decoding details do not establish changes to existing experiments.

E4.justification: Table 9 adds a focused test of whether CoT prompting improves accuracy, supplementing the existing comparisons of reasoning-tuned models. The 120-error analysis and all twelve pages of qualitative examples are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report point accuracies without repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The added results do not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Shared results in Tables 2–4 and the corresponding appendix tables are unchanged. v2 Table 9 adds CoT-condition scores, including Gemini 2.0 Flash's 60.14% synthetic and 55.88% real accuracy; five of the six model/subset averages decrease relative to standard prompting. Table 13 adds overall scores, including Gemini's 57.08%. These are additional conditions and aggregations, not version-to-version performance gains.

T1.justification: Neither version develops formal theoretical results, proofs, or derivations. The descriptive task categories remain unchanged, and v2 introduces no new mathematical analysis.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same benchmark contribution and findings: a substantial human–model gap, limited benefits from mathematical and reasoning-tuned models, and modest gains from larger or newer models.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning training data, synthetic-to-real generalization, model scaling, and perception versus numerical-intuition errors remain substantively unchanged. The added CoT paragraph reports an empirical trend without introducing a new mechanism explanation or limitation.

D1.justification: v2 substantially expands the evaluation specification: Appendix B gives image dimensions and resizing rules; Appendix C adds max_new_tokens >= 512 with other defaults, explicit prompt templates, InternVL2.5-38B answer extraction and its prompt, and details of the two human evaluators. The abstract also changes promised resource release to reported code and dataset availability. These are documentation and access-status changes, not evidence that retained experiments used different procedures.

R1.justification: v2 adds a reference for Meta's Llama 3.2 Vision Instruct, an already evaluated model. Section 2.2 also explicitly incorporates BLINK and VisOnlyQA into its discussion of reasoning and perception benchmarks. The broader research positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized grammar and wording edits, updates author order and affiliations, standardizes the benchmark name in Table 1, and inserts an evaluation-details subsection in Appendix C. The overall narrative and section organization are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds prompt Table 8, CoT-results Table 9, overall-results Table 13, and extraction-prompt Figure 10. Existing appendix displays are renumbered and reflowed; Figure 3 wording, captions, and Table 4's gain/loss colors receive limited revisions. The original visual evidence is retained.

improvement.justification: v2 makes the benchmark easier to understand and reproduce by documenting prompts, answer extraction, preprocessing, and human evaluation that v1 described incompletely. Table 9 also provides a useful direct check of prompting sensitivity. These additions improve transparency and supporting evidence while leaving the core benchmark, primary results, and conclusions unchanged.
